docs.title: Confidence intervals
docs.text: The metrics of the evaluation are reported with a confidence interval, for the whole test set and for every subgroup. The intervals come from a bootstrap, which makes no assumption about the distribution of the metric. This page explains how they are computed and what to do for the metrics that use a predictive distribution.

docs.title: The bootstrap
docs.text:
For a set of n test samples:

  1. n_bootstraps new sets of n samples are drawn with replacement. The metrics that are computed from the same kind of prediction (point predictions and probabilities, or a predictive distribution) share the same draws.
  2. Every metric is computed on every new set.
  3. The interval is made of the percentiles of these values that leave (1 - ci_level) / 2 on each side. With the default ci_level = 0.95, these are the 2.5th and the 97.5th percentiles.

The point estimate is the metric on the original test set. The draws are seeded by random_state of [workflow], so the same configuration gives the same intervals. n_jobs of [workflow] sets how many processes compute the resamples, for the metrics that need it.

The settings are in [workflow.evaluation.metrics]: n_bootstraps, ci_level and the metrics themselves. A larger n_bootstraps gives steadier bounds at the cost of time. Setting n_bootstraps = 0 skips the intervals, and the bounds are saved as NaN.

docs.title: When the bootstrap cannot be computed
docs.text:
• A resample with a single class. Some metrics, such as roc_auc and ap, are not defined when a resample has only one class, which happens with rare outcomes. Those resamples are skipped, and the interval uses the others. If every resample fails, or the test set itself has one class, the interval cannot be computed.
  • A failure in the whole computation. The evaluation does not stop. A warning is logged, the point estimates are saved, and the bounds are NaN. If the point estimates cannot be computed either, they are NaN too.

docs.title: Metrics that use a predictive distribution
docs.text: Metrics such as crps compare the observed value with the whole predictive distribution of a model like OrdBoostRegressor. A distribution object cannot be handed to the bootstrap like a column of numbers, so there are two ways to resample, and a metric uses one of them.

docs.title: Metrics with a per_sample_func
docs.text:
crps is the mean of one score per sample. Its MetricSpec has a per_sample_func that returns this score for every sample:

per_sample = per_sample_func(y_true, dist)  # shape (n_samples,)

The scores are computed once. A resample is then a draw of these scores, and its metric is their mean. This is fast, and it works with any distribution object, since the distribution is never cut into pieces.

docs.title: Metrics without one
docs.text:
For any other metric, the pairs of observed value and distribution are resampled, and the function of the metric is run again on each resample. This is exact for any metric, but slower, and the resamples are computed in parallel with n_jobs.

It needs the distribution to support row indexing, dist[indices], to build the resampled distribution. The distributions of OrdBoost 0.6.0 and later do. A distribution that does not, such as a frozen SciPy distribution, cannot be used with such a metric, and the interval fails with:

['name'] do not define a per_sample_func, so they are bootstrapped by resampling (y, dist) pairs, which requires a distribution supporting row indexing.

To avoid this, give the metric a per_sample_func. This is only valid for a metric that is the mean of a per-sample score.

docs.title: Registering a metric with a per_sample_func
docs.text:
import numpy as np

from medpipe import MetricRegistry
from medpipe.metrics import MetricSpec


def absolute_pit_error(y, dist):
    """Distance of the PIT value of each sample from 0.5."""
    return np.abs(dist.cdf(y) - 0.5)


MetricRegistry.register_spec(
    MetricSpec(
        name="pit_error",
        func=lambda y, dist: float(np.mean(absolute_pit_error(y, dist))),
        response_method="predict_dist",
        display_name="PIT error",
        per_sample_func=absolute_pit_error,
    )
)

func returns the metric on the whole test set and per_sample_func its score for each sample, so the mean of the second is the first. A metric that needs the predictive distribution can only be used with models that predict one, as explained on the regression page.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: The number of samples of the distribution has to match the number of observed values, otherwise an error is raised. For some distribution objects this check cannot be made, and the error then comes from the computation of the metric itself.

docs.title: The run folder
docs.text: Every pipeline writes what it produces in its own numbered folder. The folder holds the configuration, the environment, the fitted models, the results and the figures of the run, so a run can be inspected, restored and reproduced later.

docs.title: Where it is
docs.text:
The folder is created when the pipeline is created, not when it is run. It is named v1 in the first free place of the base folder, v2 for the next one, and so on, and a folder of an earlier run is never overwritten. The base folder is artifacts in the current directory, unless base_artifact_dir is given:

from medpipe import MedpipeClassifier

pipe = MedpipeClassifier("config.toml", base_artifact_dir="runs")
print(pipe.run_dir)  # runs/v1

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
This is the folder of a classification run in the audit mode with two outcomes, MORTALITY_30D and ANY_COMP:

artifacts/v1/
├── execution.log
├── env/
│   ├── config.toml
│   ├── env_state.json
│   └── resolved_config.json
├── models/
│   ├── MORTALITY_30D_model.joblib
│   ├── ANY_COMP_model.joblib
│   └── medpipe_classifier_demo_fitted.joblib
├── CV/
│   ├── MORTALITY_30D_cv_results.csv
│   ├── MORTALITY_30D_cv_summary.json
│   ├── ANY_COMP_cv_results.csv
│   └── ANY_COMP_cv_summary.json
├── results/
│   ├── MORTALITY_30D_evaluation_results.json
│   └── ANY_COMP_evaluation_results.json
└── plots/
    ├── MORTALITY_30D/
    │   └── MORTALITY_30D_roc_curve.png, ...
    ├── ANY_COMP/
    ├── roc_auc_strata_heatmap.png
    └── log_loss_strata_heatmap.png

The CV/ folder is only there when cross-validation was run, and plots/ when figures were drawn. The table says which run modes write what.

Content fast cv eval audit env/, execution.log, models/, results/ Yes Yes Yes Yes CV/ Yes Yes plots/ Yes Yes

docs.title: env/
docs.text:
File Content resolved_config.json The validated configuration with all the defaults filled in, and resolved_models, the model of each outcome once the overrides are applied. This is the file load() restores a pipeline from. config.toml A copy of the TOML file the pipeline was created from. It is not written when the pipeline is created from a configuration object. env_state.json The description of the environment, listed below.

env_state.json contains:

Key Content timestamp_utc When the pipeline was created. config_hash SHA-256 of the resolved configuration, which is identical for identical configurations. dataset_hash SHA-256 of the dataset file, or FILE_NOT_FOUND. A changed dataset gives a different hash. python_version, platform The Python version and the operating system. git_commit_hash The commit of the repository the code was run from, or null outside a repository.

The versions of the installed packages are not recorded. If an exact environment matters, save the output of pip freeze alongside the run.

docs.title: execution.log
docs.text: Every message of the run, down to the debug level, whatever the verbose setting of the console. Each line holds the time, the logger, the level, the place in the code and the message.

docs.title: models/
docs.text:
File Content <outcome>_model.joblib The fitted model of one outcome: the preprocessing and the estimator in a scikit-learn pipeline, wrapped by the recalibration if there is one. <project_name>_fitted.joblib A dictionary with the models of all outcomes. load() reads this file.

The files are written with joblib, which uses pickle. Only load files from runs you trust, since loading can run code. A model also needs compatible versions of scikit-learn, and of OrdBoost or NGBoost, to be loaded.

docs.title: results/
docs.text:
<outcome>_evaluation_results.json holds the metrics on the test set, with their confidence intervals. It is written by run() and by evaluate() when save_artifacts is true.

{
  "outcome": "ANY_COMP",
  "overall": {
    "roc_auc": {"point_estimate": 0.57, "ci_lower": 0.41, "ci_upper": 0.72}
  },
  "strata": {
    "SEX": {
      "F": {"roc_auc": {"point_estimate": 0.61, "ci_lower": 0.42, "ci_upper": 0.74}},
      "M": {"roc_auc": {"point_estimate": 0.27, "ci_lower": 0.17, "ci_upper": 0.43}}
    },
    "AGE": {
      "[18, 50]": {"roc_auc": {"point_estimate": 0.39, "ci_lower": 0.19, "ci_upper": 0.62}}
    }
  }
}
  • overall has one entry per metric of [workflow.evaluation.metrics].
  • strata has the same metrics for every subgroup of [workflow.evaluation.fairness]. A range is named by its two ends, [18, 50]. It is empty without a fairness configuration.
  • The bounds come from the bootstrap, as explained in confidence intervals. They are NaN (written as NaN in the file) when the intervals were not computed.

docs.title: CV/
docs.text:
Two files per outcome, written by the cross-validation:

File Content <outcome>_cv_results.csv One row per fit. Without a grid search, one row per fold with the fit and score times and a test_<metric> column. With a grid search, one row per combination of hyperparameters with scikit-learn's cv_results_: the parameters, the score of every fold (split0_test_<metric>, ...), their mean and standard deviation, and the rank. <outcome>_cv_summary.json The mean and standard deviation of each metric over the folds. For a grid search, those of the selected hyperparameters.

The scores follow the scikit-learn convention that a larger value is better, so error and loss metrics are negative. A log_loss of 0.4 is saved as -0.4. The names of the parameters are prefixed with the step of the pipeline, classifier__ or regressor__.

docs.title: plots/
docs.text: The figures of each outcome are in a folder named after the outcome, and the subgroup heatmaps are directly in plots/. The names of the files are listed with the classification and regression figures.

docs.title: Restoring a run
docs.text: MedpipeClassifier.load(run_dir) and MedpipeRegressor.load(run_dir) rebuild a pipeline from env/resolved_config.json and the models of the run. What the restored pipeline saves from then on is written in an eval folder inside the folder of the run, so the original files are never changed. An example is shown in the examples.

docs.title: Reproducing a run
docs.text:
To run an experiment again, create a pipeline from env/config.toml (or from resolved_config.json with MedpipeClassifierConfig.model_validate). With the same data, the same random_state and the same package versions, the splits and the intervals are the same. The config_hash and the dataset_hash of the new run tell whether the configuration and the data are the ones of the original.

The random_state of [workflow] is not given to the models. To reproduce a model that has some randomness, set its own random_state in the hyperparameters.

The TRIPOD+AI reporting page maps these files to the items of the reporting guideline.

docs.title: TRIPOD+AI reporting
docs.text:
TRIPOD+AI is the reporting guideline for studies that develop or evaluate prediction models built with regression or machine learning (Collins et al., BMJ 2024;385:e078378). It asks the authors to report how the data was prepared, how the model was built and validated, how it performs, and how the work can be reproduced.

MedPipe records the modelling decisions and the performance of a run, so that a large part of the checklist can be filled in from the run folder. It does not write the report, and using it does not make a study compliant with the guideline. Many items concern the study itself, such as the participants, the ethics approval or the funding, and only the authors can report them.

docs.title: What is covered
docs.text:
MedPipe is built around three parts of the checklist: the output and the performance of the model, the reproducibility of the work, and the correct handling of the data. The tables say what MedPipe provides for each topic, and where the information is. Match the topics with the items of the published checklist.

Coverage: Provided means that the information is recorded or produced by every run. Partly means that some of it is, and the rest has to be reported by the authors.

docs.title: Model output and performance
docs.text:
Topic What MedPipe provides Coverage Model output Probabilities for classifiers, and the predictive distribution for the models that have one. Metrics that need class labels use a fixed threshold of 0.5. A threshold is not chosen or tuned. Partly Discrimination The area under the ROC curve, the average precision, and the ROC and precision-recall curves. Provided Calibration The Brier score, the log loss, the integrated calibration index, and the reliability diagram. A fitted model can be recalibrated on a separate set with isotonic, sigmoid or temperature scaling. Provided Clinical usefulness The decision curve analysis, which gives the net benefit for a range of thresholds. Provided Regression performance The RMSE, the MAE and the CRPS, and the coverage, sharpness, Winkler score, marginal calibration and PIT figures of the prediction intervals. Provided Uncertainty A bootstrap confidence interval for every metric. The number of resamples and the level are in the configuration. See confidence intervals. Provided Performance in subgroups Every metric, with its interval, for each subgroup defined in [workflow.evaluation.fairness], and a heatmap of the differences with the whole test set. The groups are chosen by the user, and no fairness criterion is tested. Partly

The metrics are computed on the test set, which is kept apart from the model building. The values, with their bounds, are saved in results/<outcome>_evaluation_results.json, and the figures in plots/.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text:
Topic What MedPipe provides Coverage Specification of the experiment The original and the resolved configuration, which hold the data, the preprocessing, the algorithm and the hyperparameters of each outcome, the splits, the metrics and the subgroups. Provided Hyperparameter tuning Whether a grid search was used, the values searched, the cross-validation strategy, and the scores of every combination in CV/<outcome>_cv_results.csv. The combination is selected on the first metric of the list. Provided Identity of the data The path of the dataset, and its SHA-256 hash in env/env_state.json, so that the exact file can be identified. Provided Identity of the configuration A SHA-256 hash of the resolved configuration, in env/env_state.json. Provided Random seeds random_state of the workflow, in the configuration. The seed of a model is a hyperparameter of that model. Provided Software The Python version, the platform and the Git commit of the code, in env_state.json. The versions of the packages are not recorded. Partly The fitted models The models are saved in models/ with the configuration that built them. A run can be restored with load() and run again from its configuration. There is no export of the coefficients or of a readable equation. Partly Code MedPipe is open source under the Apache 2.0 licence. The code of the analysis is the configuration file and the script that calls the pipeline. Partly

Every run is saved in its own folder and never overwritten, so the runs of a study can be kept and compared. See the run folder.

docs.title: Correct handling of the data
docs.text:
The pipeline is built so that the performance reported on the test set is not inflated by information from the model building.

Topic What MedPipe does Coverage Separate sets The test set is set aside first, then the recalibration set, and the rest is the training set. The cross-validation and the grid search only use the training set. The recalibration set is separate from both. Provided Preprocessing The operations are part of the model. They are fitted on the training data only, also inside each fold of the cross-validation, and only applied to the other sets. Provided Validation by group The test and the recalibration sets can be defined by a column, for example the year or the hospital, which gives a temporal or geographical validation. The two sets cannot share a value, and the cross-validation can keep the groups apart in the folds. This is an internal validation, and an external validation needs a dataset from another source. Provided Leakage of the outcome A column cannot be both a predictor and an outcome, which is checked before anything is run. The columns used to split the data or to describe subgroups are not given to the model unless they are listed as predictors. Provided Class balance The cross-validation of classifiers keeps the share of positives in every fold. There is no resampling or reweighting, unless the model has a hyperparameter for it, such as class_weight. Partly Checks before the run The configuration is validated as a whole before any data is read. The columns that are needed are checked before any model is fitted. Provided Size of the sets The number of rows of each split, in execution.log. There is no calculation of the sample size needed. Partly

The other topics of the checklist, such as the participants, the definition of the outcomes and the predictors, the missing data, and the items about ethics and openness, are outside what MedPipe records. The ones to report yourself are listed at the end of this page. MedPipe does not provide an interpretation of the model, such as the importance of the predictors.

docs.title: Using the run folder for the report
docs.text:
To describe a study, the files to look at are:

  1. env/resolved_config.json for the data, preprocessing, models, hyperparameters, splits, metrics and subgroups.
  2. env/env_state.json for the dataset and configuration hashes, the Python version and the commit.
  3. CV/ for the internal validation and the tuning.
  4. results/ for the performance with the confidence intervals, overall and by subgroup.
  5. plots/ for the discrimination, calibration, decision curve and subgroup figures.
  6. execution.log for the size of each split.

docs.title: What to report yourself
docs.text:
A run does not record these items, so they have to be written in the report or kept next to the run:

  • the participants, the setting, the eligibility criteria and the dates of the data;
  • the definition and the measurement of the outcomes and of the predictors;
  • the amount of missing data and how it was handled;
  • the sample size justification;
  • the versions of the packages, for example with pip freeze;
  • the choice of the threshold used to turn probabilities into decisions;
  • the ethics approval, the funding, the conflicts of interest and the availability of the data and of the protocol.

docs.title: Configuration guide
docs.text:
A MedPipe experiment is described by a single TOML file. The file says which data to load, which models to fit, how to split and validate the data, which metrics and figures to produce, and how much to log. Because the whole experiment lives in one file, it is saved with every run and can be reused to reproduce the results.

The reference for everything that can be written in a configuration file is examples/default_classifier_config.toml. This guide explains each section of that file and shows the matching snippet.

docs.title: Loading a configuration
docs.text:
Pass the path of the file to MedpipeClassifier (or MedpipeRegressor):

from medpipe import MedpipeClassifier

pipe = MedpipeClassifier("config.toml")
pipe.run()

The file is read and validated when the pipeline is created, before any data is loaded. You can also pass an already built MedpipeClassifierConfig object instead of a path.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
The file is organised in top-level tables, one per topic:

Section Purpose Required [meta] Project name, run mode and console verbosity. Yes [data] Dataset location, predictor columns and outcome columns. Yes [default_model] Algorithm, hyperparameters and recalibration applied to every outcome. Yes [outcome_overrides.<outcome>] Per-outcome changes to the default model. No [workflow] Preprocessing, data splits, cross-validation, metrics and fairness analysis. Yes [display] Figure settings. When run_mode is "audit" or "eval"

Each section has its own page. The classifier and regressor configurations share the same layout, and the differences are described on the regression page.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
A configuration is checked as a whole, so a mistake is reported with the full path of the offending key:

1 validation error for MedpipeClassifierConfig
meta.run_mode
  Input should be 'fast', 'eval', 'cv' or 'audit' [type=literal_error, input_value='audti', input_type=str]

This is a Pydantic ValidationError. The checks that apply to every section are:

  • Unknown keys are rejected. A misspelt key is an error rather than being silently ignored. The only exceptions are [workflow.preprocessing] operations, which accept the constructor arguments of the transformer, and [display.defaults], which accepts extra plot arguments.
  • Required keys must be present. A key listed as required in the tables below has no default.
  • Rules that involve several sections (for example, a recalibration method requires a recalibration split) are reported with a message that names both.

Tip

Catch pydantic.ValidationError around the pipeline creation, as in the quickstart, to print configuration errors without a full traceback.

docs.title: [data]
docs.text:
Where the dataset is, which columns the models learn from, and which columns they predict.

[data]
path = "../tests/test_data.csv"
predictors = [
  "AGE",
  "SEX",
  "PRIOR_CANCER",
  "ADMISSION_ACUITY",
  "ADMISSION_SOURCE",
  "CATEGORY_LEVEL_1",
  "OP_SEVERITY",
]
outcomes = ["MORTALITY_30D", "ANY_COMP"]
Key Type Default Description path string required Path to the dataset file. It must have a file extension. predictors list of strings required Columns used as model inputs. outcomes list of strings required Columns to predict. One model is fitted for each outcome. kwargs table {} Extra keyword arguments passed to the file reader. See reader arguments.

docs.title: Dataset file
docs.text:
path is used as written, so a relative path is relative to the directory the script is run from, not to the configuration file. The example uses ../tests/test_data.csv, which works when it is run from the examples/ folder.

The file is read with the pandas reader that matches its extension. The extension is not case-sensitive.

Extension Reader .csv, .txt pandas.read_csv .tsv pandas.read_csv with a tab separator .parquet, .pq pandas.read_parquet .feather pandas.read_feather .xlsx, .xls pandas.read_excel .json pandas.read_json .jsonl pandas.read_json with lines=True .pkl, .pickle pandas.read_pickle

Note

Reading Excel files needs the openpyxl package, which is not installed with MedPipe. Install it with pip install "medpipe[excel]". Only load pickle files that you created yourself or trust, as unpickling can run arbitrary code.

Other formats can be supported by registering a reader with DataLoaderRegistry.

The file is not opened when the configuration is validated. A missing file, a directory, or an unsupported extension is reported when the data is loaded at the start of the run.

docs.title: Predictors and outcomes
docs.text:
Only the columns that the configuration refers to are kept from the file. All other columns are dropped when the data is loaded. Besides predictors and outcomes, the configuration can refer to columns in the following places, and these columns must exist in the file too:

  • the group_column of a split or of cross-validation (see [workflow.validation]);
  • the strata of the fairness analysis (see [workflow.evaluation.fairness]).

These extra columns are used to split the data or to describe subgroups. They are never given to the model as inputs unless they are also listed in predictors. In the example, OP_YEAR and DHB_NAME are used to split the data, and they are not among the predictors.

The following rules are checked:

  • A column cannot be both a predictor and an outcome. Otherwise the model would be given the answer, and the configuration is rejected with the list of overlapping columns.
  • Every column the configuration refers to must be present in the file. A missing column stops the run, before any model is fitted, with the list of missing columns.

Each outcome gets its own model. The models can share the same settings or be configured separately, as described in [outcome_overrides].

docs.title: Reader arguments
docs.text:
Anything under [data.kwargs] is passed to the pandas reader chosen for the file. This is useful for options such as the sheet of an Excel file or the separator of a text file:

[data]
path = "data/cohort.xlsx"
predictors = ["AGE", "SEX"]
outcomes = ["MORTALITY_30D"]

[data.kwargs]
sheet_name = "Cohort"

The arguments are not checked when the configuration is validated, so an argument the reader does not accept is reported when the data is loaded.

docs.title: [default_model]
docs.text:
The model fitted for every outcome, and the optional recalibration applied to it afterwards. Each outcome gets its own fitted copy, so outcomes share these settings but not the fitted model.

[default_model]
algorithm = "HistGradientBoostingClassifier"

[default_model.hyperparameters]
learning_rate = 0.1
loss = "log_loss"
max_features = 0.2

[default_model.recalibration]
recalibrate = true
method = "isotonic"

[default_model.recalibration.hyperparameters]
y_min = 0.0
y_max = 1.0
out_of_bounds = "clip"
Key Type Default Description algorithm string required Name of the model class. See available models. hyperparameters table {} Arguments passed to the model constructor. recalibration table none Recalibration applied after the model is fitted. Omit it to fit the model without recalibration.

docs.title: Algorithm
docs.text:
algorithm is the exact class name of an estimator from scikit-learn (sklearn.ensemble, sklearn.linear_model, sklearn.isotonic), NGBoost or OrdBoost, or of a model you registered with ModelRegistry. The models page lists where names are looked up and how to register your own.

The name is looked up when the configuration is validated, so a misspelt name is reported before any data is loaded. A model registered with ModelRegistry is accepted if it is registered before the pipeline is created.

docs.title: Hyperparameters
docs.text:
Every key under [default_model.hyperparameters] is passed to the constructor of the model. A key the model does not accept is reported when the model is created.

A hyperparameter can be a list of values to search over:

[default_model.hyperparameters]
learning_rate = [0.1, 0.05]
max_depth = 10

When grid_search = true in [workflow.validation.cross_validation] and the run mode runs cross-validation, every combination of the listed values is tried and the best model is kept. Scalar values are held fixed. Without a search, the first value of a list is used. See the run modes.

docs.title: Recalibration
docs.text:
Recalibration adjusts the predicted probabilities of a fitted classifier so that they match the observed frequencies better. The model is first fitted on the training set, then a calibrator is fitted on a separate recalibration set.

Key Type Default Description recalibrate boolean required Whether to recalibrate the fitted model. method string "isotonic" "isotonic" (isotonic regression), "sigmoid" (Platt scaling) or "temperature" (temperature scaling). hyperparameters table {} Reserved for hyperparameters of the recalibration method. Currently not used. See the note below.

Note

The hyperparameters of the recalibration are accepted by the configuration but are not used yet: they are not passed to the recalibration method, and any values are ignored. A future version may pass them directly to the recalibrator, for example y_min, y_max and out_of_bounds for the isotonic method. Until then, only recalibrate and method have an effect.

The recalibration set is defined by [workflow.validation.recalibration_split]. A recalibration table in the default model requires that split, even when recalibrate = false. To disable recalibration, either omit the recalibration table or set recalibrate = false and keep the split.

docs.title: [display]
docs.text:
The figures produced for each outcome. This page describes the figures of a classifier. The regressor has its own defaults and figures, which are described on the regression page. The table is required when run_mode is "audit" or "eval", the modes that produce figures, and it can be left out otherwise.

[display.defaults]
n_bootstraps = 1000
save = true
show = false
n_bins = 10
dist_n_bins = 25
dist_yscale = "log"
strategy = "uniform"

[display.overrides.calibration]
n_bootstraps = 10

[display.outcome_overrides.ANY_COMP.reliability]
strategy = "quantile"

[display.theme]
dpi = 300
Key Type Default Description defaults table all defaults Settings used by every figure. overrides table none Settings for one type of figure, for all outcomes. outcome_overrides table none Settings for one type of figure, for one outcome. theme table none Fonts, colours and resolution of the figures.

The figures of each outcome are saved in the plots/<outcome>/ folder of the run, and the subgroup heatmaps in plots/. For a classifier these are:

Figure File Plot type ROC curve <outcome>_roc_curve.png roc Precision-recall curve <outcome>_pr_curve.png precision_recall Reliability diagram (calibration curve) <outcome>_reliability_diagram.png reliability Histogram of the predicted probabilities <outcome>_data_distribution.png data_distribution Decision curve analysis <outcome>_dca_curve.png dca Subgroup heatmap, one per metric <metric>_strata_heatmap.png strata_heatmap

The heatmaps are only drawn when [workflow.evaluation.fairness] is defined. Each has one row for the whole test set and one for every subgroup, and one column for every outcome. The text is the value of the metric, and the colour is how far the value is from the one of the whole test set.

docs.title: [display.defaults]
docs.text:
Settings that apply to every figure.

[display.defaults]
n_bootstraps = 1000
save = true
show = false
n_bins = 10
dist_n_bins = 25
dist_yscale = "log"
strategy = "uniform"
Key Type Default Description n_bootstraps integer 1000 Number of bootstrap resamples for the 95% confidence bands of the curves. With 0, the bands are not drawn. save boolean true Whether the figure is saved in the run folder. show boolean false Whether the figure is displayed in a window. n_bins integer 10 Number of bins of the reliability diagram. strategy string "uniform" How the reliability diagram is computed: "uniform" (bins of equal width), "quantile" (bins with the same number of samples) or "spline" (a smooth curve fitted with splines). cv_splines integer 3 Number of internal folds of the spline fit, 2 or more. Only used when strategy is "spline". dist_n_bins integer 10 Number of bins of the histogram of the predicted probabilities. It is also used for the histogram drawn under the reliability diagram. dist_yscale string "linear" Scale of the y-axis of these histograms: "linear", "log", "symlog" or "logit". n_jobs integer 1 Number of parallel jobs for the bootstrap of the figures. It is independent of workflow.n_jobs.

Note

The histograms have their own dist_n_bins and dist_yscale. n_bins only applies to the reliability diagram.

docs.title: [display.overrides] and [display.outcome_overrides]
docs.text:
The defaults can be changed for one type of figure with overrides, and for one type of figure of one outcome with outcome_overrides. Both use the same keys as defaults, and only the keys that are written are changed.

# Changes the calibration figures of all outcomes
[display.overrides.calibration]
n_bootstraps = 10

[display.overrides.roc]
n_bootstraps = 500

# Changes the reliability diagram of ANY_COMP only
[display.outcome_overrides.ANY_COMP.reliability]
n_bootstraps = 50
strategy = "quantile"

For a given figure, the settings are combined in this order, and the last one wins:

  1. [display.defaults]
  2. [display.overrides.<plot type>]
  3. [display.outcome_overrides.<outcome>.<plot type>]
  4. The arguments given when a plot method is called in Python.

The plot type is the name of the figure in the table below. Each type also has aliases, which can be used in any of the tables, and the different names of a type are combined.

Plot type Aliases Keys that have an effect roc roc_curve n_bootstraps, n_jobs, save, show precision_recall pr, pr_curve n_bootstraps, n_jobs, save, show reliability calibration, reliability_diagram n_bins, strategy, cv_splines, dist_n_bins, dist_yscale, n_bootstraps, n_jobs, save, show data_distribution distribution, dist dist_n_bins, dist_yscale, save, show dca dca_curve save, show strata_heatmap heatmap save, show

The name of the outcome in outcome_overrides must be in data.outcomes. A plot type that is not in the table is rejected. A key that has no effect for a plot type, such as n_bins for the ROC curve, is accepted and ignored.

docs.title: [display.theme]
docs.text:
The look of all the figures.

[display.theme]
primary_color = "#2D90D8"
ci_alpha = 0.3
dpi = 300
font_family = "sans-serif"
show_grid = false
Key Type Default Description primary_color string "#2D90D8" Colour of the curves and bars. The heatmaps have their own colour scale. palette list of strings five colours Reserved for figures that draw several series. Currently not used. ci_alpha float 0.3 Opacity of the confidence bands, between 0 and 1. linewidth float 2.0 Width of the curves. dpi integer 300 Resolution of the saved images. font_family string "sans-serif" Font of the titles, labels and ticks. title_fontsize integer 12 Size of the titles. label_fontsize integer 10 Size of the axis labels. show_spines boolean false Whether the top and right borders of the axes are drawn. show_grid boolean false Whether a grid is drawn.

A key that is not in the table is rejected. Colours can be written as hexadecimal codes or as any colour name that Matplotlib accepts.

docs.title: [meta]
docs.text:
General information about the run.

[meta]
project_name = "medpipe_classifier_demo"
run_mode = "audit"
verbose = 1
Key Type Default Description project_name string required Name of the project. It cannot be empty. It is used to name the saved pipeline file, <project_name>_fitted.joblib. run_mode string "audit" Which stages of the pipeline are run. See run modes. verbose string, integer or boolean "compact" How much is printed to the console. See verbosity.

docs.title: Run modes
docs.text:
The run mode controls whether the models are tuned with cross-validation and whether figures are produced. Models are always fitted on the training set, evaluated on the test set, and saved.

run_mode Cross-validation Figures Typical use "fast" No No Quick checks while setting up a configuration. "cv" Yes No Tuning and comparing models without producing figures. "eval" No Yes Producing figures for models whose settings are already chosen. "audit" Yes Yes The full run, for reporting.

The run mode also decides which sections must be present:

  • [workflow.validation.cross_validation] is required in "cv" and "audit", the modes that run cross-validation.
  • [display] is required in "audit" and "eval".

Note

A list-valued hyperparameter (for example learning_rate = [0.1, 0.05]) is a grid to search over when grid_search = true in a mode that runs cross-validation. In "fast" and "eval" there is no search, and the first value of the list is used.

Every run is written to a new, numbered folder (artifacts/v1, artifacts/v2, and so on). The folder always contains the models, the evaluation results, the resolved configuration, the environment description and the execution log. Cross-validation results (CV/) are added in "cv" and "audit", and figures (plots/) in "eval" and "audit".

docs.title: Verbosity
docs.text:
verbose only changes what is printed to the console. The execution log saved in the run folder always records everything, down to the debug level.

Level Accepted values Console output Quiet "quiet", "warning", 0, false Warnings and errors only. Compact "compact", "progress", 1 The main steps of the run (data loading, fitting, evaluation). Info "info", "detailed", 2, true Every informational message. Debug "debug", 3 Everything, including internal details.

To change the verbosity for a single run without editing the file, pass verbose_override when creating the pipeline:

pipe = MedpipeClassifier("config.toml", verbose_override="debug")

docs.title: [outcome_overrides]
docs.text:
The default model is used for every outcome unless an outcome is overridden. An override is written as a table named after the outcome, for a column listed in data.outcomes:

[outcome_overrides.ANY_COMP]
algorithm = "GradientBoostingClassifier"

[outcome_overrides.ANY_COMP.hyperparameters]
learning_rate = [0.1, 0.05]
max_depth = 10

[outcome_overrides.ANY_COMP.recalibration]
recalibrate = false

An override has the same keys as [default_model], and all of them are optional. Only the keys that are written change the default model, so an override can, for example, change a single hyperparameter or only switch the recalibration off:

[outcome_overrides.ANY_COMP.hyperparameters]
max_depth = 5

[outcome_overrides.MORTALITY_30D.recalibration]
method = "sigmoid"

The name of an outcome that is not in data.outcomes is rejected. Outcomes without an override use the default model unchanged.

docs.title: How an override is combined with the default
docs.text:
The settings of an override are applied on top of the default model, one group of settings at a time.

Algorithm and hyperparameters

  • If the override uses the same algorithm as the default, or has no algorithm, its hyperparameters are merged into the default ones. Keys that are present in both take the override value, and the other default keys are kept.
  • If the override uses a different algorithm, the default hyperparameters are discarded and only the hyperparameters written in the override are used. This avoids passing arguments that the new model does not accept.

For example, with the default model above:

Override Resulting hyperparameters algorithm = "HistGradientBoostingClassifier", learning_rate = 0.5 learning_rate = 0.5, loss = "log_loss", max_features = 0.2 algorithm = "RandomForestClassifier", n_estimators = 50 n_estimators = 50 algorithm = "RandomForestClassifier" none, so the model defaults are used

Recalibration

  • If the override has no recalibration table, the default recalibration is kept, even when the algorithm changes.
  • If the override has the same method as the default, or no method, the keys it sets replace the default ones. Its hyperparameters are merged into the default ones.
  • If the override has a different method, the default recalibration hyperparameters are discarded and only those written in the override are used. recalibrate is kept from the default unless the override sets it.
  • If the default model has no recalibration, an override that adds one must set recalibrate.
  • Setting recalibrate = false in an override turns the recalibration off for that outcome.

In the example above, ANY_COMP uses a different algorithm and disables recalibration. MORTALITY_30D has no override and uses the default model with isotonic recalibration.

Whenever the default model has a recalibration table, or an override turns recalibration on for an outcome, [workflow.validation.recalibration_split] must be defined.

docs.title: Regression
docs.text:
A regression experiment uses the same configuration file layout as a classification experiment, and is run with MedpipeRegressor instead of MedpipeClassifier:

from medpipe import MedpipeRegressor

pipe = MedpipeRegressor("config.toml")
pipe.run()

The file is validated against MedpipeRegressorConfig. This page lists what is different from the classification configuration described in the other pages of this guide. Everything that is not mentioned here works in the same way.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Section Difference [meta] None. [data] None. The outcomes are continuous columns. [default_model] and [outcome_overrides] No recalibration. The algorithms are regressors. [workflow.validation] Different cross-validation splitters. The recalibration split is accepted but not used. [workflow.evaluation] Different metrics and defaults. No cv_splines. [display] Different defaults and figures.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
A regression model has an algorithm and its hyperparameters, and nothing else. A recalibration table is not part of a regression model, and it is rejected in [default_model] and in the overrides.

[default_model]
algorithm = "OrdBoostRegressor"

[default_model.hyperparameters]
n_bins = 10
mapper = "quantile"
learning_rate = 0.1
max_iter = 100
random_state = 42

The algorithm is looked up in the same places as for classification, so any regressor of scikit-learn, NGBoost or OrdBoost can be used, as well as the models you registered with ModelRegistry. Overrides work as described in [outcome_overrides], without the recalibration rules.

Two of the models can predict a full distribution of the target instead of a single value. This is what the crps metric and most of the figures need.

Model Predicts a distribution Figures OrdBoostRegressor Yes Yes NGBRegressor Yes No Other regressors, such as LinearRegression No No

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
[workflow.validation] has the same keys. The differences are:

  • Cross-validation: the splitters of the random and group strategies are not stratified, since there are no classes to keep in proportion. They are KFold and GroupKFold. The loso strategy is the same.
  • Recalibration split: recalibration_split is accepted, but regression models are not recalibrated, so nothing uses the rows. They are only removed from the training set. Leave the table out unless you need the rows to be set aside.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
[workflow.evaluation.metrics] has the same keys, with these differences:

Key Default Description metrics ["rmse", "mae"] Metrics to compute. cv_splines not available Only used by the ici metric, which is for classifiers. The key is rejected.

The metrics for regression are:

Name Description Needs rmse Root mean squared error. Any regressor mae Mean absolute error. Any regressor crps Continuous ranked probability score. A model that predicts a distribution

The metrics are checked against the type of outcome when the configuration is validated. A classification metric such as roc_auc or accuracy is rejected, since it cannot be computed on continuous values. crps is rejected if the algorithm of any outcome cannot predict a distribution, for example LinearRegression. rmse and mae are accepted with any regressor.

The [workflow.evaluation.fairness] table works as for classification. The metrics are computed for each subgroup, and the heatmaps are drawn from them.

docs.title: Display
docs.text: [display] has the same structure, and the same overrides, outcome_overrides and theme tables, with the following differences. The table is still required when run_mode is "audit" or "eval".

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
[display.defaults]
n_bootstraps = 1000
save = true
show = false
dist_n_bins = 20
dist_yscale = "linear"
coverage_levels = [5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, 85, 95]
pit_n_bins = 20
Key Type Default Description n_bootstraps integer 1000 Number of bootstrap resamples for the 95% confidence bands of the coverage, sharpness and Winkler score curves. With 0, the bands are not drawn. save boolean true Whether the figure is saved in the run folder. show boolean false Whether the figure is displayed in a window. n_jobs integer 1 Number of parallel jobs for the bootstrap of the figures. It is independent of workflow.n_jobs. dist_n_bins integer 20 Number of bins of the histogram of the target values. dist_yscale string "linear" Scale of the y-axis of that histogram: "linear", "log", "symlog" or "logit". coverage_levels list of numbers 5 to 95 in steps of 10 Nominal coverage of the prediction intervals, in percent, evaluated by the coverage, sharpness and Winkler score curves. Each level must be strictly between 0 and 100. pit_n_bins integer 20 Number of bins of the PIT histogram.

The keys of the classification defaults that only concern classifiers, n_bins, strategy and cv_splines, are rejected. Unlike for classification, other keys are rejected too.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Plot type Aliases Figure File Keys that have an effect coverage coverage_curve Share of true values inside the prediction intervals <outcome>_coverage.png n_bootstraps, n_jobs, coverage_levels, save, show sharpness sharpness_curve Mean width of the prediction intervals <outcome>_sharpness.png n_bootstraps, n_jobs, coverage_levels, save, show winkler winkler_curve, winkler_score Winkler score of the intervals <outcome>_winkler.png n_bootstraps, n_jobs, coverage_levels, save, show marginal_calibration marginal_calib Marginal calibration curve <outcome>_marginal_calibration.png save, show pit_histogram pit Histogram of the probability integral transform <outcome>_pit_histogram.png pit_n_bins, save, show data_distribution distribution, dist Histogram of the target values <outcome>_data_distribution.png dist_n_bins, dist_yscale, save, show strata_heatmap heatmap Subgroup heatmap, one per metric <metric>_strata_heatmap.png save, show

The classification plot types, such as roc and calibration, are rejected. The settings are combined in the same order as for classification: the defaults, then overrides, then outcome_overrides, then the arguments given in Python.

[display.overrides.coverage]
coverage_levels = [50, 80, 95]

[display.outcome_overrides.LOS_DAYS.pit]
pit_n_bins = 10

The first six figures are only drawn for models that predict a distribution through OrdBoost, as shown in the table of models. For any other model, a warning is logged for the outcome and its figures are skipped, but the run goes on and the evaluation results are saved as usual. The subgroup heatmaps only need the evaluation results, so they are drawn for every model when [workflow.evaluation.fairness] is defined. Errors in the units of the target (rmse, mae and crps) have a colour scale that follows the data, instead of the fixed scale used for metrics between 0 and 1.

docs.title: Using the pipeline
docs.text:
MedpipeRegressor has the same run, fit, evaluate, plot_all and load methods as MedpipeClassifier. The prediction methods are different:

MedpipeClassifier MedpipeRegressor predict: class labels predict: predicted values predict_proba: class probabilities predict_dist: predictive distribution, for the models that have one decision_function none

docs.title: Complete example
docs.text:
The repository contains a configuration that uses every block, examples/default_regressor_config.toml. It is run by examples/minimal_regressor_example.py on the data of tests/test_regression_data.csv. A shorter configuration looks like this:

[meta]
project_name = "length_of_stay"
run_mode = "audit"
verbose = 1

[data]
path = "data/cohort.csv"
predictors = ["AGE", "SEX", "OP_SEVERITY"]
outcomes = ["LOS_DAYS"]

[default_model]
algorithm = "OrdBoostRegressor"

[default_model.hyperparameters]
n_bins = 10
mapper = "quantile"
learning_rate = 0.1
max_iter = 100
random_state = 42

[workflow]
random_state = 42
n_jobs = 2

[workflow.validation.test_split]
strategy = "random"
test_size = 0.2

[workflow.validation.cross_validation]
strategy = "random"
n_splits = 3

[workflow.evaluation.metrics]
metrics = ["rmse", "mae", "crps"]
n_bootstraps = 200

[workflow.evaluation.fairness]
strata = ["SEX"]

[display.defaults]
n_bootstraps = 200
coverage_levels = [50, 80, 95]

docs.title: [workflow]
docs.text:
How the data is prepared, split and validated, and how the fitted models are evaluated. This is the largest section, so it is divided into sub-tables, each described below.

[workflow]
random_state = 42
n_jobs = 2

[workflow.preprocessing]
# ...

[workflow.validation.test_split]
# ...

[workflow.evaluation.metrics]
# ...
Key Type Default Description random_state integer 42 Seed for the random parts of the pipeline. Must be 0 or more. n_jobs integer 1 Number of parallel jobs. Use -1 for all processors. preprocessing table none Transformations applied to the predictors. validation table required How the data is split and cross-validated. evaluation table required Metrics, confidence intervals and subgroup analysis.

random_state seeds the random train/test and recalibration splits, the shuffling in cross-validation, and the bootstrap resampling of the confidence intervals. Running the same configuration on the same data therefore gives the same splits and intervals. It is not passed to the models. To fix the randomness of a model, set the model's own random_state in its hyperparameters.

n_jobs sets the parallelism of cross-validation, grid search and the bootstrap resampling. It does not affect the plots.

docs.title: [workflow.preprocessing]
docs.text:
Transformations that are applied to the predictors before they reach the model.

[workflow.preprocessing]
preprocess = true
operations = [
  { name = "OrdinalEncoder", columns = ["SEX", "ADMISSION_ACUITY", "ADMISSION_SOURCE", "CATEGORY_LEVEL_1"] },
  { name = "StandardScaler", columns = ["CATEGORY_LEVEL_1", "AGE"], with_mean = true },
]
Key Type Default Description preprocess boolean none Whether the operations are applied. When it is false or the table is omitted, the predictors are given to the model unchanged. operations list of tables none The operations, applied in order. Required when preprocess is true.

Each operation is a table with the following keys:

Key Type Description name string Class name of the transformer. See available preprocessing operations. columns list of strings Predictors the operation is applied to. It cannot be empty. any other key any Passed to the constructor of the transformer, such as with_mean above.

The operations are applied one after the other, each one to its own columns. All the other columns are passed on unchanged. In the example, the four categorical predictors are first encoded as numbers, and CATEGORY_LEVEL_1 and AGE are then scaled. A column can be used by several operations.

Some points to keep in mind:

  • columns must be listed in data.predictors. An operation on any other column is rejected when the configuration is validated, with a message that names the operation and the columns.
  • columns always refers to the original name of a predictor. A later operation cannot refer to a column that an earlier operation replaced with several columns, such as the output of a OneHotEncoder.
  • The operations are fitted as part of the model, so during cross-validation they are fitted on the training folds only.
  • The operation names and their arguments are only checked when the data is prepared. An unknown name or an argument the transformer does not accept stops the run at that point.

docs.title: [workflow.validation]
docs.text:
How the data is divided. The test set is set aside first. If a recalibration split is defined, the recalibration set is taken from what remains, and the rest is the training set. Cross-validation is then run on the training set only.

all data ──► test set
         └─► remaining ──► recalibration set (optional)
                       └─► training set ──► cross-validation folds
Key Type Default Description test_split table required The held-out test set. recalibration_split table none The set used to recalibrate the models. Required when recalibration is used. cross_validation table none Cross-validation on the training set. Required when run_mode is "cv" or "audit".

docs.title: test_split
docs.text:
[workflow.validation.test_split]
strategy = "group"
group_column = "OP_YEAR"
values = [2024]
Key Type Default Description strategy string "random" "random" or "group". test_size float none Fraction of the data used for testing, strictly between 0 and 1. Required for "random". group_column string none Column that defines the groups. Required for "group". values list of strings or integers none Values of group_column that go to the test set. Required for "group".
  • With the "random" strategy, rows are assigned to the test set at random, using random_state. The split is not stratified.
  • With the "group" strategy, every row whose group_column value is in values is in the test set, and all the other rows are not. This is useful for temporal or geographical validation, for example to test on the most recent year or on a hospital that was not used for training.

docs.title: recalibration_split
docs.text:
[workflow.validation.recalibration_split]
strategy = "group"
group_column = "OP_YEAR"
values = [2023]
Key Type Default Description strategy string required "random" or "group". It must be the same as the test split. recalibration_size float none Fraction of the data left after the test split that is used for recalibration, strictly between 0 and 1. Required for "random". group_column string none Required for "group". It must be the same as in the test split. values list of strings or integers none Values of group_column that go to the recalibration set. Required for "group". None of them can also be in the test split.

The recalibration split follows the same logic as the test split, and has to be consistent with it. For example, with test_size = 0.3 and recalibration_size = 0.2, the test set has 30% of the data, the recalibration set has 20% of the remaining 70%, and the training set has the rest. The recalibration split is required whenever recalibration is enabled for a model.

docs.title: cross_validation
docs.text:
[workflow.validation.cross_validation]
strategy = "group"
grid_search = true
group_column = "DHB_NAME"
n_splits = 3
shuffle = true
Key Type Default Description strategy string required "random", "group" or "loso". n_splits integer none Number of folds, 2 or more. Required for "random" and "group". Not used for "loso". group_column string none Column that defines the groups. Required for "group" and "loso". shuffle boolean true Whether to shuffle the data before it is divided into folds. The shuffling uses random_state. grid_search boolean none Whether to search over the list-valued hyperparameters.

The strategies are:

Strategy Folds Classifiers Regressors "random" n_splits folds of random rows StratifiedKFold, which keeps the share of positives in every fold KFold "group" n_splits folds in which a group is never split between folds StratifiedGroupKFold GroupKFold "loso" One fold per group, each holding out a single group (leave one group out) LeaveOneGroupOut LeaveOneGroupOut

The models are scored on every metric in workflow.evaluation.metrics.metrics. What happens next depends on grid_search:

  • grid_search = true: every combination of the list-valued hyperparameters is tried. The best combination is chosen using the first metric of the metrics list, and the model is refitted with it on the whole training set.
  • Otherwise: the cross-validation only reports the scores. The model is then fitted on the whole training set, using the first value of every list-valued hyperparameter.

The fold scores are saved in the CV/ folder of the run. Cross-validation is only run when run_mode is "cv" or "audit".

docs.title: [workflow.evaluation]
docs.text: How the fitted models are evaluated on the test set.

docs.title: metrics
docs.text:
[workflow.evaluation.metrics]
metrics = ["roc_auc", "log_loss"]
n_bootstraps = 50
ci_level = 0.95
Key Type Default Description metrics list of strings ["roc_auc", "ici"] Metrics to compute. See the list of available metrics. n_bootstraps integer 200 Number of bootstrap resamples used to compute the confidence intervals. Use 0 to skip the intervals. ci_level float 0.95 Confidence level of the intervals, between 0 and 1. cv_splines integer 3 Number of internal folds used by the spline fit of the ici metric, 2 or more. Lower values are faster. It has no effect on other metrics.

Every metric is computed on the test set with a bootstrapped confidence interval. The names are checked when the configuration is validated, so a metric you registered with MetricRegistry is accepted if it is registered before the pipeline is created. The metrics are also checked against the type of outcome: for a classifier, a metric that needs a predictive distribution (crps) is rejected. The regression page lists the rules for regressors.

The results are saved for each outcome in results/<outcome>_evaluation_results.json, with the point estimate and the bounds of the interval for every metric:

{
  "outcome": "MORTALITY_30D",
  "overall": {
    "roc_auc": {"point_estimate": 0.61, "ci_lower": 0.42, "ci_upper": 0.74}
  },
  "strata": {}
}

The strata entry has the same values for each subgroup of the fairness analysis.

With n_bootstraps = 0 the bootstrap is skipped: only the point estimates are computed, and ci_lower and ci_upper are saved as NaN.

docs.title: fairness
docs.text:
Optional. Computes the metrics on subgroups of the test set, to check whether the model performs equally across patient groups. The results are also drawn as heatmaps when figures are produced.

[workflow.evaluation.fairness]
strata = ["SEX", "AGE"]
groups = { "AGE" = [[18, 50], [51, 120]] }
Key Type Default Description strata list of strings required Columns that define the subgroups. groups table none Ranges to use for some of the strata.

For every column in strata:

  • If the column is not in groups, there is one subgroup for each distinct value of the column. In the example, SEX gives one subgroup per sex.
  • If the column is in groups, each entry is a [minimum, maximum] range, and both ends are included. In the example, AGE gives the subgroups [18, 50] and [51, 120]. Every entry must have exactly two values.

A key of groups must also be in strata, and its list cannot be empty. Ranges are for numeric columns. To make subgroups of a categorical column, leave it out of groups.

The strata columns have to exist in the data, but they do not have to be predictors. A column that is only used for the fairness analysis, for example a hospital, is read from the data but never given to the model. A column that is missing stops the run before any model is fitted.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: MedPipe requires Python 3.12 or later.

docs.title: Standard installation
docs.text:
Install the published package from PyPI:

pip install medpipe

Check that the installation worked:

python -c "import medpipe; print(medpipe.__version__)"

docs.title: Optional dependencies
docs.text:
Reading Excel files (.xlsx and .xls) needs the openpyxl package, which is not installed by default. Install it with the excel extra:

pip install "medpipe[excel]"

docs.title: Installing from source (developer setup)
docs.text:
To set up a local development environment and contribute to MedPipe, clone the GitHub repository:

git clone git@github.com:Surgical-Recovery-and-Safety-Lab/medpipe.git
cd medpipe

Install the package in editable mode with the development dependencies:

pip install -e ".[dev]"

The dev extra includes the test tools (pytest) and the docs extra (mkdocs, linting and type-checking tools). To preview this documentation locally:

mkdocs serve

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Once the package has been installed, try the quickstart example.

docs.title: MedpipeClassifier simple example
docs.text:
Use MedpipeClassifier to create a pipeline for a classification task. The pipeline is defined by a TOML configuration file, which is validated when the pipeline is created.

from pydantic import ValidationError

from medpipe import MedpipeClassifier

try:
    pipe = MedpipeClassifier("default_classifier_config.toml")
    pipe.run()
except ValidationError as err:
    print(err)
    exit()

The configuration file used above is examples/default_classifier_config.toml. It shows everything that can be written in a classification configuration, and each block is described in the configuration guide. Run the example from the examples/ folder, since the paths in the configuration are relative to where the script is run.

docs.title: MedpipeRegressor simple example
docs.text:
Use MedpipeRegressor for a continuous outcome. The pipeline is defined in the same way, by a TOML configuration file.

from pydantic import ValidationError

from medpipe import MedpipeRegressor

try:
    pipe = MedpipeRegressor("default_regressor_config.toml")
    pipe.run()
except ValidationError as err:
    print(err)
    exit()

The configuration file is examples/default_regressor_config.toml. It predicts the length of stay and the blood loss with OrdBoostRegressor, which predicts a full distribution of each outcome. The regression page of the guide lists how a regression configuration differs from a classification one.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Each run is saved in a new numbered folder, artifacts/v1, artifacts/v2, and so on. It contains the fitted models, the evaluation results with confidence intervals, the figures, and the configuration and environment of the run. The run folder page describes each file.
